title: indigo_mount_ioptron: MOUNT_STATE slew light never shows a coordinates ALERT
description: Audit in 1078b2c4: the slew light is never set to ALERT. Owner's rule (decided 2026-11-22 for mount_synscan, ticket 1078b2c4, and extended to this driver on 2026-11-23): whenever MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES is in ALERT, the SLEW light of MOUNT_STATE is ALERT too; BUSY while the coordinates are BUSY; otherwise as before. The library keeps a coordinates ALERT until the next BUSY (indigo_update_coordinates() kept-ALERT rule, indigo_reject_coordinates_change()), so the light must be derived from the coordinates state after indigo_update_coordinates() has decided it, at every place the driver publishes the coordinates or MOUNT_STATE (poll, refusals, sync, abort, park/home, connect), not from the driver's own motion flags alone. Reference implementation: synscan_update_mount_state() and its call order in indigo_drivers/mount_synscan/indigo_mount_synscan.driver (commit 5f794cc15). Scope: the .driver source (version bump, regenerate with the unchanged generator), simulator-backed cases proving the light follows the coordinates state through a refused/failed request (ALERT kept while idle), the next accepted request (BUSY, then OK/IDLE) and connect, adaptation of existing cases that asserted IDLE under a kept ALERT, recorded run with tools/run_driver_test.py, MIGRATION_STATUS count. Refusals inserted by the generator (parked/homing guards) cannot call driver code; if the light lags there until the next poll, record it in the ticket note and do not change the generator.

outcome.summary: No required changes. MOUNT_STATE is now published once per poll after the coordinates via the whole-property fingerprint (PARK/HOME/TRACKING lights still published); all writers run on the device queue; generated files byte-identical to regeneration with the current generator; the connect check fails 2/2 without the init_mount line; adapted cases legitimate. Non-blocking: comment on ioptron_slew_light says 'after indigo_update_coordinates()' while the on_change call is deliberately before the generated publication; MOUNT_STATE goes out just before the coordinates on that path; parked-guard refusal lags until the next poll (no dedicated case); build/bin/indigo_generator in the primary checkout is stale and must be rebuilt before regenerating there. Not verified: Linux, Windows, TCP suite, hardware.

history.text: Deriving the SLEW light from the published coordinates state in the .driver
Building the driver and the ioptron simulator test
Running the new slew light cases with a case filter

Cause: the status poll set MOUNT_STATE_SLEW_ITEM only from the controller's slew flag (BUSY while slewing, IDLE otherwise) and published MOUNT_STATE before indigo_update_coordinates(), so a refused GOTO, a failed sync, an aborted GOTO, a slew ended short of the target or a failing position readback left the coordinates ALERT (kept by the library) with an IDLE light. Fix (indigo_mount_ioptron.driver version 71 -> 72, regenerated .c with the unchanged generator, .h/_main.c unchanged): ioptron_slew_light() derives the light from the coordinates state (ALERT -> ALERT, BUSY or controller still slewing -> BUSY, else IDLE); ioptron_update_slew_light() sets it and publishes MOUNT_STATE only when its fingerprint changed. Called after indigo_update_coordinates() in the poll (MOUNT_STATE is now published after the coordinates instead of inside the polled loop, still only on change), at the end of the MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES on_change (the result follows the BUSY published by INDIGO_COPY_TARGETS_PROCESS_COORDINATES_CHANGE, so the generated indigo_update_coordinates() publishes it unchanged) and after the 'Slew aborted' publication; ioptron_init_mount() sets the light from the coordinates state before MOUNT_STATE is defined. Behaviour change beyond IDLE->ALERT: after an abort during a slew the light is ALERT instead of BUSY while the mount decelerates. Known lag: the generator-inserted parked guard (indigo_reject_coordinates_change 'Mount is parked!') cannot call driver code, the light follows at the next poll (<= 1 s); not changed, not covered by a dedicated case. Tests (indigo_test/integration/test_mount_ioptron_simulator.c): new ioptron_slew_light_follows_coordinates_8406/_0205/_0300 (HC8406, V2.5, V3 protocols): (a) refused GOTO (injected MS/MS1 refusal) -> coordinates ALERT and light ALERT, held 2.5 s (>= 2 idle polls) with no other SLEW light published; same for a refused sync (injected Sd reply 0); (b) next accepted GOTO -> coordinates BUSY and a BUSY light publicati

Proof of failure without the fix: the three new cases run (INDIGO_TEST_CASE_FILTER=slew_light) against the pre-fix driver (HEAD .driver/.c restored temporarily and rebuilt) fail 3/3 at wait_light(SLEW, ALERT) after the refused GOTO; with the fix 3/3 pass. Recorded run: python3 tools/run_driver_test.py mount_ioptron -> 2026-11-23 15:03 3.0.0.72 mac arm64 simulator 144/144 OK (README + TEST_SUMMARY written by the script). MIGRATION_STATUS mount_ioptron 144 -> 147 (144 serial cases + 3 opt-in TCP cases, not run here). flow check passed (whitespace; unit not selected). Not verified: Linux, Windows, opt-in TCP suite, sanitizer build, MountSim, hardware.
